Subject: Operational Measurement Checklist — Availability & Latency Evidence

Hi Sean,

Thanks for the demo last week — ClearWave’s infra and procurement teams are aligned and we need a short packet describing exactly how Redwood measures and reports availability and latency for hosted inference. Procurement has prepared a short checklist and a follow-up meeting request. High level asks:

- How is uptime defined and measured (windowing, p95/p99, synthetic vs real traffic)?
- What monitoring and alerting hooks are available to customers (read-only dashboards, alert forwarding, webhook payloads)?
- Sampling and telemetry: what percentage of real requests are recorded in dashboards and retained for audits?
- Exception policy: if Redwood requests a temporary SLO carveout, what is the process and evidence required?

We’d like the packet by EOD Friday so we can feed it to our security and procurement teams. I attached the checklist we use to make sure nothing is missed.

Best,
Sara Lin
Director, Procurement
ClearWave Analytics

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Operational Measurement Checklist — Availability & Latency Evidence

Sara — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a concise evidence matrix and short explainer to address each bullet. Summary up front:

1) Uptime definition: we report platform availability as the percent of successful model-inference responses over a rolling 30-day window, excluding planned maintenance windows and customer-configured regional outages. Availability = successful responses / total requests (2xx responses), measured at the load-balancer boundary. We also publish a monthly availability figure for contract compliance.

2) Latency measurement: we publish p50/p90/p95/p99 for end-to-end server-side latency (time from request ingress to final token produced). Latency buckets break out by model family, sequence-length class (short <128, medium 128-1024, long >1024), and region. For contract tables we use p95 over a 30-day rolling window as the primary SLA metric.

3) Synthetic vs real telemetry: we operate both synthetic probes and real-user telemetry. Synthetic probes exercise end-to-end stacks from multiple regions every 5 minutes; these are used for alerting and runbook drills. Real-user telemetry (production requests) feeds the official SLA calculations. We maintain tagged synthetic vs synthetic-excluded filters in telemetry so they do not affect contractual metrics.

4) Sampling & retention: default recording captures 100% of error traces and 10% of successful request traces for detailed inspection; aggregated metrics (counts/latencies) are computed at 100% fidelity for SLO math. Raw traces retained for 90 days; aggregated stats retained for 13 months for audit requests.

5) Customer access: we provide read-only Grafana links for SLO dashboards, and optional Grafana viewer invites tied to customer Master Account IDs. We also offer an API endpoint and a webhook for SLO alert notifications (payload sample in attachment).

6) Exception / carveout policy: temporary exceptions (e.g., sampling changes, maintenance-induced monthly variance) require a written Mutual Action Plan, customer acceptance, and an agreed evidence packet. Exceptions are time-limited (typically 7–30 days) and documented as amendments to the service order.

I’ve included a short draft mutual action plan and the evidence matrix (redwood-slo-evidence-matrix.xlsx) with example exports and synthetic probe configs. Marissa — can you confirm the forensic exports we can provide for audit? Karthik — can you own the commercial wording for a 30-day provisional exception?

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-min sync if that helps.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Sara / Sean — quick confirmation on exports: for audits we can deliver the following artifacts in the evidence packet (PDF/CSV bundle):

- Aggregated SLO timeseries (30d window) by model, region, seq-length class (CSV)
- Raw error traces for any flagged incident (redacted for PII) (JSON/NDJSON)
- Synthetic probe history (timestamps, region, probe-type) — 90 days (CSV)
- Grafana dashboard snapshots and a one-click read-only invite (link + viewer account creation instructions)
- Runbook excerpts showing alert thresholds, escalation paths, and incident RCA templates

We will redact any customer payload data and provide checksums for delivered files. For the SLA calculation, note that transient transient KV cache misses are included in server-side latency metrics; we can also provide a cache-hit breakdown for deeper analysis.

If ClearWave needs direct streaming access to metrics to feed their observability, we can open a read-only Prometheus scrape endpoint (scoped) under a short-term agreement — typically used during procurement review and then revoked post-procurement.

I propose a two-step delivery: 1) high-level packet (this week) and 2) full quarantine export for procurement/legal within 10 business days.

—Marissa

Sara — clarifying commercial/exceptions language for procurement:

- Standard SLA: 99.95% monthly availability (rolling 30d), p95 latency target (region/model-specific) per SOW. Remedies: service credits computed pro rata per incident bucket.
- Temporary exception: Redwood may propose a limited SLO variance for planned migrations or model-quantization rollout; exceptions require mutual sign-off (Document: Mutual Action Plan) and specify monitoring, rollback criteria, and observation windows.
- For procurement timelines: we accept a short-term compliance carveout during onboarding (max 30 days) with a documented acceptance of risk by ClearWave.

If that sounds acceptable, Sean/Marissa will supply the technical evidence and we’ll include one paragraph in the SOW draft for the carveout process and evidence expectations.
